results.title: DENR Express Permitting on Wheels serves 10,000 clients in first 5 months
results.description: By replacing costly travel, bureaucratic delays, and repeated trips to regional offices with mobile hubs and face-to-face technical assistance, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources’ (DENR) flagship project ‘DENR Express: Permitting on Wheels’ served more than 10,000 clients and issued thousands of permits across the country in its first five months since implementation in April 2026. DENR Secretary Juan Miguel “Mitch” Cuna said the DENR Express was established to bring environmental permitting, technical assistance and compliance guidance closer to communities, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and project proponents. The initiative addresses a common challenge faced by applicants, particularly those living far from regional offices, as securing environmental permits and clearances could mean spending on transportation and accommodation, and making repeated trips when applications had incomplete requirements or technical deficiencies. Cuna said the DENR Express directly responds to the directive of President Marcos to make government services more accessible and responsive to the public. The President’s directive is reflected in the program’s approach of bringing government personnel, technical assistance and permitting services directly to cities and municipalities instead of requiring stakeholders to travel to government offices. DENR Express mobile service hubs provide face-to-face assistance, real-time document validation, guidance in using online application systems and, for eligible applications, accelerated processing of certain permits and clearances. From April to August 2026, DENR Express assisted 10,776 clients nationwide. During the same period, the program issued 2,852 environmental permits and clearances. These included: 194 Environmental Compliance Certificates (ECCs); 682 Certificates of Non-Coverage (CNCs) for Category D projects or those unlikely to cause significant adverse environmental impacts; 595 Pollution Control Officer (PCO) accreditations; 473 Wastewater Discharge Permits; 423 Hazardous Waste Generator (HWG) ID registrations; 379 Permits to Operate (PTOs); 85 Permits to Transport (PTTs); and 21 Chemical Control Order (CCO) registrations. Beyond permit and clearance issuance, DENR Express also provided 2,302 direct assistance transactions to help applicants navigate government systems and address technical, regulatory and administrative concerns. These included assistance with Self-Monitoring Report and Compliance Monitoring Report online systems, company registration, cashier payment services, legal inquiries and records requests. The program has also shortened the processing time for several environmental regulatory services. PCO accreditation, for instance, was reduced from an average of 14 days to two days, a 12-day reduction. This allows establishments to designate their environmental officers sooner and helps prevent delays in subsequent compliance monitoring and reporting. Processing of Hazardous Waste Generator IDs was likewise reduced from seven to two days, while CNC processing was cut from six days to three days. ECC processing, meanwhile, was reduced from 13 days to 10 days. These gains are made possible in part by the program’s face-to-face approach. Technical personnel can immediately identify incomplete requirements or other deficiencies and explain to applicants how these can be addressed, reducing the need for repeated trips to DENR or Environmental Management Bureau (EMB) offices. While the figures refer primarily to permits issued by the EMB, the Permitting on Wheels also brings together other DENR offices for other services such as tree cutting permitting, land patent issuance, and addressing inquiry concerns on mining, wildlife, and the like. Cuna earlier underscored how the DENR Express changes that approach by bringing permitting services directly to citizens on a regular basis, saying, “Instead of stakeholders going to the government, the DENR is bringing its services closer to the citizens, across different LGUs.” Clients served range from homemakers to wildlife owners to company Pollution Control or Environmental Officers. But beyond providing frontline services, DENR Express also serves as a feedback mechanism for the agency. Issues encountered by applicants during onsite activities can be documented and used to improve online systems, guidance materials, documentary requirements and administrative workflows, where allowed under existing policies. The DENR intends to sustain and institutionalize DENR Express as a regular government service through appropriate policy issuances, regular deployment and stronger coordination with local government units and other government agencies. Through the initiative, the DENR aims to make environmental compliance easier to access while maintaining the safeguards required by law. By bringing technical assistance and permitting services closer to communities, DENR Express helps reduce unnecessary travel, repeated transactions and delays, supporting economic activity while promoting responsible environmental management.
